title: Don't Settle Too Early: Self-Reflective Remasking for Diffusion Language Models
claim: The model can revise its own earlier mistakes by remasking low-confidence tokens, and this ability yields better results than existing models across many benchmarks.
layout: 2 panels side by side: left, a vertical stack of four text rows read top to bottom with a 'denoising steps' arrow; right, a radar chart with a legend
description: The figure has two panels. Panel (a) on the left shows one sentence fragment ('Calculate how many grapes were left for the pies') at four successive denoising steps, with a grey downward arrow labeled 'denoising steps'. Tokens sit on colored highlights: green for tokens already unmasked, red for tokens being remasked, blue for tokens newly unmasked, grey for tokens still masked. The word 'left' first appears in blue. It is then struck through in red and remasked. It then shows grey, and finally becomes 'used' in blue. Panel (b) on the right is a radar chart with six axes: HumanEval, MBPP, ARC-C, IFEval, AlpacaEval, GSM8K and MATH. The axes are grouped under the arcs Code, General Tasks and Mathematics. Three translucent polygons compare LLaDA (red), Dream (purple) and RemeDi (blue). The blue RemeDi polygon encloses the other two. The eye goes first to the highlighted text rows, then to the large blue radar.
caption: (a) Illustration of remasking for quality improvement: RemeDi initially predicts the token “left”, but later identifies a semantic mismatch in the phrase “left for the pies”. The model then remasks this token and corrects it to the more appropriate “used”. (b) RemeDi outperforms existing DLMs in various tasks, including math, code and general benchmark.
abstract: Mask-based Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) struggle to revise incorrect tokens: once a token is generated, it typically remains fixed. The key challenge is to identify potential errors in the inputs. In this paper, we propose \emph{\underline{Rem}asking-\underline{e}nabled \underline{Di}ffusion Language Model (RemeDi}, a mask-based DLM that introduces \emph{remasking} as another fundamental mechanism, enabling more flexible text refinement in diffusion-based text generation. To achieve this, RemeDi jointly predicts token distributions and per-token confidence scores at each step. The confidence scores determine which tokens to be unmasked after the current step, allowing the model to identify tokens with low quality and remask them. These remasked tokens can be resampled with richer context in subsequent steps. We design a remask-aware pipeline to train this ability, including supervised fine-tuning which teaches the model to detect and remask incorrect tokens in addition to predict mask tokens, and reinforcement learning which optimizes full generation trajectories toward higher rewards. Experiments show that RemeDi achieves the state-of-the-art results among open-source DLMs on multiple datasets.
